The proposed gate changes the recurrence beyond the GRU reset gate. With q_t=g_t⊙h_previous, the cell computes its reset/update gates and candidate from q_t, and its carry term becomes z_t⊙g_t⊙h_previous (using z as retention). Standard reset gating affects candidate construction; update gating mixes the previous state with the candidate. Thus, by algebraic inspection, this adds state attenuation before every recurrent computation, including the carry path. It supplies no new contextual information: standard GRU gates already condition on e_t and h_previous. Structural difference alone establishes neither novelty nor benefit. See [GRU equations](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1412.3555).

Related mechanisms include [Gated Feedback RNNs](https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.02367), which condition recurrent communication gates on current inputs and previous states, and [CARNN](https://aclanthology.org/N18-1115/), which uses external context to regulate information flow; neither establishes priority for this exact construction. [Recurrent Highway Networks](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/zilly17a/zilly17a.pdf) initialize transform gates toward closed, favoring carry, while [chrono initialization](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11188) initializes recurrent gate biases around intended memory timescales. For this extra multiplicative gate, a reasonable proposed initialization is W_e=W_h=0 and b=logit(0.99)≈4.60, recovering approximately the underlying GRU initially. This preserves the baseline computation, not necessarily identity dynamics; saturation slows gate learning, as discussed in [gate-refinement work](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.09890).

Recommended comparisons: standard GRU at identical width; wider GRU matched on total trainable parameters; g≡1; learned constant-vector, input-only, and hidden-only gates; and zero-bias versus near-open initialization. Parameter-controlled recurrent comparisons have precedent in [Chung et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1412.3555). Keep training, tuning budgets, seeds and evaluator fixed; report macro validation HR@10, runtime, gate saturation and history-length sensitivity. Existing papers do not establish recommendation gains for this exact gate.
